user.task_schema:
RadGraph directed-relation schema:
- Modify: one observation modifies another observation, or one anatomy entity modifies another anatomy entity.
- LocatedAt: an observation is located at or associated with an anatomy entity.
- SuggestiveOf: one observation is suggestive of another observation.
Annotate only relations expressed within the FINDINGS and IMPRESSION sections.
Relations are directed from subject to object. Select endpoints only from immutable_entities; never create or alter an entity.

[R01]
Domain: relation
Priority: 1
Instruction: Project every relation onto the supplied predicted-entity inventory. A relation endpoint must be the ID of one supplied predicted entity; never invent an ID, create a composite span, or return a human-annotation ID.
Applies when: Selecting or aligning either endpoint of any relation.
Exceptions: ["Minor punctuation or boundary differences may be normalized when a predicted entity clearly denotes the same concept.", "A predicted entity may be used despite an observation-label disagreement if its span and concept clearly match.", "If an annotated multiword endpoint is split into several predicted entities, select the single semantic head appropriate to the relation. Additional modifier-to-head relations may be emitted only when independently licensed by the text.", "If no predicted entity represents a required endpoint, omit that relation rather than substituting a neighboring entity or collapsing a relation path."]
Examples: ["A location spanning a regional qualifier plus an organ maps to the supplied organ-head entity, while the regional qualifier may separately Modify the organ.", "If a positional predicate is not supplied as an entity, do not replace it with the finding and manufacture a direct positional relation."]

[R02]
Domain: relation
Priority: 2
Instruction: Emit directed triples with exactly one allowed predicate: LocatedAt, Modify, or SuggestiveOf. Preserve subject and object roles; do not add inverse, symmetric, or transitive relations. Emit an exact triple only once.
Applies when: Formatting and validating all relation outputs.
Exceptions: ["The same endpoint pair may receive different predicates only when distinct textual semantics independently support both labels.", "Repeated mentions in different sentences or report sections are separate entities and may receive analogous relations without being duplicates."]
Examples: ["A finding-to-organ location does not license the inverse organ-to-finding triple.", "A qualifier-to-finding relation and a finding-to-site relation form a path; they do not imply qualifier-to-site."]

[R03]
Domain: relation
Priority: 3

Exceptions: ["Copular or anatomy-first predications retain state -> anatomy direction.", "Adjective-first fragments containing laterality, regional qualifiers, coordination, or additional content retain state -> anatomy direction.", "Summary or IMPRESSION restatements retain state -> anatomy direction."]

,\" emit clear -> lungs.", "For the IMPRESSION fragment \"Clear lungs.\", emit Clear -> lungs.", "For \"

,\" emit Clear -> lung."]

Priority: 7
Instruction: Attach each explicit modifier to the semantic or grammatical head of its phrase rather than to the nearest compatible entity. When a phrase-level or property modifier occurs in an anatomical phrase containing a semantically transparent depiction/container noun such as silhouette or region plus an explicit anatomy-bearing owner or more specific appositive head, use that anatomy-bearing entity as the Modify object.

\" emit left -> airspace, not left -> retrocardiac.", "In \"the

[R08]
Domain: relation
Priority: 8
Instruction: Use SuggestiveOf for an explicit evidential or interpretive link from an observed sign, finding, structure, or state to a possible diagnosis, explanation, consequence, or clinical interpretation. Domain: relation
Priority: 9
Instruction: For an explicit inferential statement with alternatives, emit one SuggestiveOf relation from the stated source to each eligible supplied interpretive target.
Applies when: One finding is explicitly said to represent, suggest, or be consistent with multiple alternatives.
Exceptions: ["Do not create a SuggestiveOf edge to an alternative represented only by an anatomical entity.", "A bare list joined by an ambiguity marker is insufficient when no explicit source finding and inferential predicate are present.", "If only one alternative has a usable supplied entity, emit only that projectable relation."]
Examples: ["single imaging finding -> first possible diagnosis and single imaging finding -> second possible diagnosis", "If one alternative is only an anatomical structure

s a condition, retain only the condition as a SuggestiveOf target."]

[R10]
Domain: relation
Priority: 10
Instruction: Relation annotation is independent of assertion status. Preserve valid LocatedAt, Modify, and SuggestiveOf links for present, absent, uncertain, stable, or negated findings.
Applies when: A relation-bearing phrase occurs under negation, uncertainty, or an absence label.
Exceptions: ["Negation does not by itself license a relation; the underlying semantic link must still be explicit.", "Do not convert negation words into relation endpoints unless they are supplied entities and function as genuine modifiers."]
Examples: ["absent effusion -> pleural compartment", "acute qualifier -> absent abnormality", "absent opacities -> possible diagnosis when the sentence explicitly states what such opacities would suggest"]

[R11]
Domain: relation
Priority: 11
Instruction: Resolve shared scope conservatively. A common state or modifier may relate to multiple coordinated entities when grammar clearly places all conjuncts within its scope.
Applies when: A predicate follows or precedes a coordinated list of findings, structures, or properties.
Exceptions: ["Do not extend the predicate to a nearby entity outside the coordination.", "Do not assume that a relation applying to one repeated finding automatically applies to all other mentions."]
Examples: ["one normality state -> each explicitly coordinated organ property", "one unremarkable state -> each member of an anatomical list", "one finding -> general site and a more specific site when both are explicitly asserted"]

[R12]
Domain: relation
Priority: 12
Instruction: Keep relation resolution local. Prefer entities in the same noun phrase, clause, or explicit predicate-argument construction, and do not perform unsupported cross-sentence or cross-section coreference.
Applies when: A possible relation would require resolving a pronoun, an omitted noun, a distant repeated concept, or an antecedent in another section.
Exceptions: ["Repeated findings in a summary section may be annotated independently using the entities and wording present in that section.", "A relation may cross a short clause boundary only when the source and target are explicitly connected by the sentence's grammar."]
Examples: ["Do not connect an earlier lesion to a later diagnosis expressed only through an unannotated pronoun.", "Annotate a repeated summary finding with its own summary-site entity rather than linking it to the earlier site mention."]

[R13]
Domain: relation
Priority: 13
Instruction: When a supplied positional or projection predicate is an entity, preserve it as an intermediate relation node. Link the positional predicate to its anatomical destination with LocatedAt, and use Modify for its direct compositional attachment to the finding or device component.
Applies when: The text contains a supplied entity corresponding to projecting, overlying, or another positional relation.
Exceptions: ["Do not collapse the path into a direct finding-to-site relation unless the text independently states that direct location.", "If the positional entity is unavailable, omit relations requiring it rather than replacing it with an adjacent entity.", "Use the grammatical descriptive dependency for the Modify edge; do not infer both directions."]
Examples: ["positional predicate -> destination structure via LocatedAt", "positional predicate -> device tip via Modify when the predicate describes the tip", "finding and positional predicate form a compositional edge only when both are supplied entities"]

[R14]
Domain: relation
Priority: 14
Instruction: Choose the predicate by semantic precedence: explicit diagnostic interpretation selects SuggestiveOf; explicit spatial or host anchoring selects LocatedAt; descriptive or compositional dependence selects Modify.
Applies when: A candidate pair appears compatible with more than one relation label.
Exceptions: ["Multiple labels may be retained only if separate explicit constructions support separate meanings.", "Entity labels alone never determine the predicate.", "Corpus-specific direction anomalies should not override the dominant semantic direction unless the local text unambiguously requires it."]
Examples: ["A lesion described as nodular receives Modify from the morphology term, but a possible nodule interpretation receives SuggestiveOf.", "An anatomical adjective on a lesion is a location anchor, whereas the same adjective on an anatomical head is a modifier."]

[R15]
Domain: relation
Priority: 15
Instruction: Avoid relation overgeneration. Do not annotate mere adjacency, shared topic, comparison with a prior study, examination recommendations, notification statements, or transitive consequences of already emitted relations.
Applies when: No explicit grammatical, spatial, descriptive, or inferential link connects two supplied entities.
Exceptions: ["Measurements and explicit temporal-status descriptors are valid Modify relations.", "Explicit report-summary restatements are valid independent relation contexts."]
Examples: ["A recommended imaging region is not automatically related to the finding prompting the recommendation.", "A modifier attached to a finding does not inherit the finding's anatomical location.", "Two findings listed in the same sentence receive no relation solely because they co-occur."]

[RA009]
Domain: relation
Priority: 7
Instruction: Do not emit Modify when the subject functions only as an epistemic or metalinguistic assessment of a concept's reality, determinacy, or clinical significance rather than as a descriptive attribute of that concept.
Applies when: A supplied term such as "true," "indeterminate," or "unknown" qualifies whether a finding is real or interpretable, or comments on its clinical significance.
Exceptions: ["Retain Modify for explicit morphology, measurement, severity, temporal status, and scalar degree descriptors, including terms such as rounded, nodular, stable, significant, and borderline.", "This rule does not suppress a relation independently licensed by an explicit descriptive use of the same word."]
Examples: ["Do not emit true -> nodule in \"

.\"", "Continue to emit rounded -> opacity and measurement -> opacity when explicitly stated."]

[RA025]
Domain: relation
Priority: 8
Instruction: For SuggestiveOf only, when the same lexical source head and same lexical target head restate one interpretation in multiple report sections, emit exactly one relation. Prefer the occurrence in which both endpoints are explicitly linked within the same inferential clause; if multiple occurrences are equally local and explicit, retain the earliest occurrence.
Applies when: Findings, Impression, or another summary section repeats the same source-to-interpretation assertion using separate supplied entity mentions.
Exceptions: ["Retain separate relations when either the source head or target head differs, or when the later occurrence expresses a distinct interpretation rather than a restatement.", "Do not merge relations merely because their targets are clinically related; the repeated target head must be the same."]
Examples: ["If Findings links prominence to lymphadenopathy only through anaphoric \"

\" and Impression directly states \"prominence ... representing ... lymphadenopathy,\" retain only the Impression relation.", "If both Findings and Impression directly state that opacities could represent pneumonia, retain only the earlier Findings relation.", "Do not merge nodules -> disease with nodules -> metastases because the target heads differ."]

[RA041]
Domain: relation
Priority: 7
Instruction: Resolve quantitative Modify attachments by the measurement construction’s semantic scope rather than proximity: a measurement associated with a generic carrier phrase such as "area of <finding>" modifies the embedded finding head, while a dimension noun in a scalar-change complement such as "

" modifies the change-state entity; attach the change state to the finding separately when explicitly licensed.
Applies when: A supplied measurement or dimension entity participates in an explicit measurement, measuring, or scalar-change construction and multiple same-clause Modify objects are available.
Exceptions: ["Do not redirect nonquantitative morphology or shape modifiers; in \"

,\" round continues to modify area.", "A property noun in an owner compound, such as \"heart size,\" is not a scalar-change complement and remains governed by the ordinary phrase-head rule.", "Emit only relations whose required endpoints are supplied entities."]
Examples: ["In \"
,\" emit size -> increased and independently increased -> density; do not attach size directly to density.", "In \"

,\" emit 6 mm -> opacity and nodular -> opacity."]

[RA047]
Domain: relation
Priority: 7
Instruction: Emit Modify from a supplied relational carrier or spacing noun to the supplied head of an explicit same-phrase complement when that complement defines the carrier's content or boundaries, as in "X of Y" or "X between Y."
Applies when: Both endpoints are supplied entities from the same semantic family (observation-to-observation or anatomy-to-anatomy), X is a generic relational noun such as "area" or "interspace," and an explicit "of" or "between" phrase makes Y the content or boundary-defining head of X.
Exceptions: ["Do not apply when the complement instead expresses the anatomical location or owner of a finding, such as \"

hemidiaphragm\"; use the independently licensed location rule.", "Do not apply when the prepositional phrase merely spatially locates an unrelated finding or when the complement head is not a supplied entity.", "For a coordinated boundary phrase, target the supplied common head and do not invent a composite endpoint or additional endpoints."]
Examples: ["In \"
,\" emit area -> density with Modify, independently of round -> area.", "In \"
